source: AWS Open Data Terrain Tiles, Terrarium encoding
rights: AWS Open Data Terrain Tiles (Mapzen/Tilezen). United States 3DEP (formerly NED) and global GMTED2010 and SRTM terrain data courtesy of the U.S. Geological Survey; global ETOPO1 terrain data U.S. National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration. Public domain sources in this area; attribution per https://github.com/tilezen/joerd/blob/master/docs/attribution.md
horizontal_crs: EPSG:26910 (NAD83 / UTM zone 10N); tiles are WGS84 Web Mercator, datum shift (~1 m) ignored
vertical: metres; 3DEP 1/3 arc-second in the United States, ETOPO1 offshore, as mosaicked by Terrain Tiles
note: Replaces the 3DEP ImageServer request (blocked from the cloud sandbox). Samples are bilinear from the z13 tile mosaic (~15 m pixels) at each raw cell centre.

aoi.description: Mendocino AVA bounding box (UC Davis AVA Project, CC0) padded by 2 km; ~58 x 63 km. Frame for the viewer, not a geological boundary.
aoi.name: Mendocino

raw.note: sampled on the fly from cached tiles in data/raw/tiles/, not stored

pit_floor.note: Along the shoreline at the frame's west edge the terrain tiles have narrow pits, down to about -4,800 m, where land and sea data meet. In this frame the tiles put the whole sea at 0 m (no bathymetry), and no land lies below sea level, so tile pixels below -100 m are treated as pits and set to 0 m. The count is recorded in data/manifest.json.
pit_floor.rule: tile pixels below this height are set to 0 m before sampling
